question.text: Yamuna Growth AIF is finalising its audit calendar. Which set of audits does an AIF typically undertake?

answer.text: Only a statutory audit of books of accounts by a CA, once every three years.
Only an internal audit by the Compliance Officer, annually.
Only a PPM audit by a merchant banker, once in the lifetime of the fund.
Annual statutory audit by a qualified auditor, an annual PPM audit performed by a CA or CS, and internal audits — per SEBI (AIF) Regulations and relevant circulars.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Chapter 7, statutory auditors, PPM auditors and internal auditors are appointed by AIFs. All books of accounts of the AIF must be audited annually by a qualified auditor, and the PPM audit is mandated each year and must be performed by a CA or CS. The Trap: Option A wrongly stretches the statutory audit interval to three years. Option B ignores both the statutory and PPM audits. Option C wrongly limits the PPM audit to a one-time event. Note: Annual PPM audits are a key compliance requirement, and any observed violations are required to be intimated to SEBI through the prescribed channel.
